<article class="proj">
<figure class="proj-banner"><img src="../images/projects/offshore-wind-hydrogen-om.svg" alt="" width="640" height="360"></figure>
<div class="proj-layout">
<div class="proj-main">
<div class="proj-glance">
<p class="glance-role"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>First author</p>
<ul class="glance-tags" aria-label="Scale and methods"><li>Gulf of Mexico wind area</li><li>Houston refinery hydrogen demand</li><li>Monte Carlo maintenance simulation</li><li>Two-stage optimization</li><li>54 sensitivity scenarios</li></ul>
</div>
<section class="proj-q" aria-labelledby="h-question">
<h2 id="h-question"><i class="bi bi-question-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Research question</h2>
<p class="proj-question">How much does prognostics-based operation and maintenance change the cost of an offshore wind farm supplying electrolytic hydrogen?</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-insight" id="insight" aria-labelledby="h-insight">
<h2 id="h-insight"><i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key insight</h2>
<p class="insight-title">A large maintenance saving became a small hydrogen-cost saving</p>
<p>Prognostics-based maintenance lowered wind operation-and-maintenance cost by about 10% and downtime by about 11%. The saving applies to the turbines alone, so its effect on the whole system was smaller: the levelized cost of hydrogen fell by about 2%.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-contribution">
<h2 id="h-contribution"><i class="bi bi-person-check" aria-hidden="true"></i>My contribution</h2>
<p>First author. I did most of the work: I linked an operation-and-maintenance simulation, developed with my co-authors, to the system techno-economic optimization, ran the analysis and did the writing.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" id="approach" aria-labelledby="h-approach">
<h2 id="h-approach"><i class="bi bi-tools" aria-hidden="true"></i>How I approached it</h2>
<ol class="approach">
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>Maintenance strategy and system design were optimized in separate models.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>I took the expected maintenance cost and turbine downtime from the maintenance optimization and used them as inputs to the system sizing and dispatch model.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>This traced the effect of maintenance through to the levelized costs of hydrogen and electricity.</p></li>
<li class="ap-card"><p class="ap-challenge"><span class="ap-k">Challenge</span>An offshore hydrogen plant needs a realistic site, buyer and price signal.</p><p class="ap-did"><span class="ap-k">What I did</span>I placed the system in a federal Gulf of Mexico wind energy area, estimated Houston-area refinery hydrogen demand from the capacities of ten refineries, and used Houston load-zone prices.</p><p class="ap-why"><span class="ap-k">Why it mattered</span>This tied the case study to a designated site and an existing demand centre.</p></li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" id="choices" aria-labelledby="h-choices">
<h2 id="h-choices"><i class="bi bi-signpost-split" aria-hidden="true"></i>Design choices</h2>
<dl class="choices">
<div class="choice"><dt>Apply prognostics-based maintenance only to the wind turbines</dt><dd><span class="ch-alt">Alternatives considered: applying it to the hydrogen equipment as well</span>Condition monitoring and prognostics are more mature for offshore wind than for hydrogen assets.</dd></div>
</dl>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-method">
<h2 id="h-method"><i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i>Method</h2>
<p>Two-stage approach: Monte Carlo operation-and-maintenance simulation, then techno-economic optimization for a Gulf of Mexico site supplying Houston-area refineries.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec" aria-labelledby="h-findings">
<h2 id="h-findings"><i class="bi bi-lightbulb" aria-hidden="true"></i>Key findings</h2>
<ol class="findings">
<li>Prognostics-based maintenance lowered wind operation-and-maintenance cost by about 10% and downtime by about 11%.</li>
<li>At the system level, the levelized cost of hydrogen fell by about 2%.</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="proj-sec proj-bounds" aria-labelledby="h-bounds">
<h2 id="h-bounds"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>Boundary conditions</h2>
<p>Single site and one weather year; maintenance parameters from the collaborators&#x27; framework.</p>
</section>
<section class="proj-next" id="led-to" aria-labelledby="h-next">
<h2 id="h-next"><i class="bi bi-arrow-right-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i>What it led to</h2>
<p>These plant studies took the site as given; where hydrogen assets should go across a whole grid became the question of my Texas study. <a class="next-link" href="txh2.html">Hydrogen&#x27;s role in expanding renewable energy in Texas<i class="bi bi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></a></p>
</section>
